results.title: STROBE-Equity Extension Checklist and Elaboration
results.content: However, the consideration of health equity is outside the scope of the STROBE statement.18 Health equity is achieved when everyone has an equal and fair opportunity to attain optimal health.19 Evidence consistently demonstrates that certain groups consistently experience barriers to achieving health equity arising from unequal access to resources and opportunities.20,21 These barriers are exacerbated by structural inequities that manifest as uneven power and privilege distribution, disadvantaging certain groups based on their living and working conditions, personal and social characteristics (eg, gender, age, ethnicity, occupation).3,22-24 International agreements have called for the development of standards for health equity-relevant research to promote health equity.25 Despite this, data suggests that inequitable experiences are often poorly reported in observational studies, leaving many population groups underrepresented in the health literature.
